newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco, union reach Sudbury deal - source.
newsitem.headline: Inco, union reach Sudbury deal - source.

text.p: Canadian nickel giant Inco Ltd has reached a tentative agreement with the union representing 4700 workers at its Ontario division, a company source said on Friday.

"We will be announcing that we and the union have reached a tentative agreement on a new three-year contract and the union leadership is unanimously recommending its approval," the source said in a telephone interview.
Unionized workers at Inco's Sudbury and Port Colbourne operations were set to go on strike at midnight on Saturday, May 31.
On Monday, the Steelworkers requested the assistance of a provincial mediator after talks reached an impasse last weekend.
Union members had voted 98 percent in favor of giving union leaders the mandate to strike if a tentative agreement could not be reached by May 31.
The contract affects 4,700 workers at the nickel giant's mining, smelting and refinery operations in Sudbury and its refinery in Port Colborne.

According to Inco's production plan for the current fiscal year, the Ontario division is expected to produce about 230 million pounds of nickel, about 200 million pounds of copper, and about four million pounds of cobalt.
